_note: The committed, machine-readable release policy for this application. Every field
here is READ AND VALIDATED by release/lib/policy.mjs before release/lib/decide.mjs
evaluates anything, and every field is decision-bearing: an invalid policy is one
refusal (policy.invalid) naming every problem. release/README.md explains the
reasoning for a human and is documentation, NOT the gate (D08-A2).
The gate and the publisher read THIS FILE FROM THE DEFAULT BRANCH, never from the
candidate: a candidate that supplied its own policy could relax its own gate. The
publisher additionally runs the verifier pinned to the exact revision the gate ran
and refuses (preflight.policy_advanced) if release/ on the default branch has moved
since, so changing anything here takes effect only on a fresh publication run.
The certifying workflow is resolved by PATH, through the GitHub API, and only
then compared with what the triggering event claimed. `workflow_run.workflows`
can match a workflow's mutable DISPLAY NAME and nothing else, so the name in
publish.yml is a coarse pre-filter GitHub forces on us — never the proof.
requiredChecks names the jobs inside that workflow whose success IS the
certification. A missing check is refused exactly as a failed one is.
A certification describes a moment. A candidate older than certificationWindowHours
is not promoted on its old statement; it is re-certified.
assessmentWindowHours is the MAXIMUM AGE of the fresh dependency assessment (D08
B2.2): the gate queries the advisory database again, over the candidate's RETAINED
lock graph, the pinned scanner and the prepared publisher toolchain, and the
publisher refuses to use the credential once that collection is older than this, or
once an applied exception record has lapsed — re-checked in its critical section and
again immediately before the credential is read. It is measured from when the
collection STARTED, never from a re-decision: re-deciding old evidence with today's
clock is not a fresh query. It cannot exceed 24 hours.
Neither window is audit evidence on its own. The certified payload is never rebuilt
as a substitute for scanning what it was built from.
THE configuration that ships. CI and the certifying run build this and nothing
else, and the publisher refuses an artifact stamped with any other name.
`uat` is the honest name for it: it carries the UAT-targeted API origin, which
is the destination this stack has today and which Stage B deliberately does NOT
change. It is not 'production' and this file does not call it that. The
environment it bakes sets Angular's `production` flag FALSE — recorded in every
manifest as environment.productionFlag so the diagnostic behaviour that follows
from it is a written-down fact rather than a discovery.
expectedApiUrl and forbiddenOriginsInBundle are asserted against the BUILT
BYTES by `release/cli.mjs stamp`, not against the source. A file replacement
that silently failed would otherwise produce an artifact that passes every
check and points at the wrong API.
The destination, pinned — and the ONLY configuration the publish tool is given.
The gate reads firebase.json AND .firebaserc at the certified commit, resolves the
destination the way firebase-tools does (release/lib/hosting.mjs), refuses anything
outside a narrow allow-list, proves every certified file survives the effective
ignore set, and the publisher then hands the tool a REGENERATED pair built from
these values. Its digest is part of the admitted record.
ignore must equal the certified firebase.json entry exactly; a change there is a
reviewed change to this file, never a silent override. publicDirectory is where
the verified payload is staged beside the regenerated configuration.
identityOrigin is the canonical Firebase site origin for this target and is where
the served identity is read back from. It is NOT a claim that it is the only
origin serving this content: which custom domains are mapped, and how a printed
diner QR URL stays valid, is an owner inventory item. Nothing here redirects,
reroutes or reprints anything.
verification is how long the publisher waits for the origin to serve the admitted
identity after the tool returns: `attempts` reads, the n-th after n x intervalMs.
Only the WAIT is configurable — what counts as verified is not.
THE PUBLICATION TOOLCHAIN, pinned as a reviewed graph rather than a version string.
release/publisher/package.json + package-lock.json are the ONLY source it is
installed from: by the gate (which holds no credential), with the pinned scanner's
npm and lifecycle scripts disabled. The gate measures the result (content tree,
entrypoint, installed inventory), assesses its graph under the dependency-audit
policy, and retains it as its own artifact; the publish job downloads THAT artifact
by id and runs `entrypoint` with the exact Node below. Nothing in the job that holds
the credential resolves, downloads or installs a tool — the app's own firebase-tools
devDependency certifies nothing about this one, and there is no `npx`, no `latest`
and no ambient `firebase` on PATH.
A checksum identifies bytes; a passing scan is not proof of safety. Changing any of
these values, or the lock, is a reviewed change and advances the verifier, so a run
admitted under the old values is refused (preflight.policy_advanced).
deployAgent is the FIREBASE_DEPLOY_AGENT label the tool is given, replacing the one
the retired action set; it is telemetry, not authority.
Where the reviewed storage compatibility declaration lives. The gate reads it
from git at the certified commit (and at a bootstrap baseline), never from the
candidate upload. See the declaration file and release/lib/storage.mjs.
Nothing on this path has ever published an identity file, so the first
publication has nothing to order itself against and no served storage
declaration to be compatible with. Both are supplied by an EXPLICIT, reviewed
owner decision: authorized true AND servedBaseline naming the commit whose build
is live (its storage declaration is then read from git). Until both are set, a
candidate the gate cannot place in order is refused (served.bootstrap_unauthorized,
storage.bootstrap_baseline_missing).
This is the frontend naming ITS OWN baseline; it is not serving evidence for a
peer. The same pull request that authorizes it should revert it once an identity
is served.
Eligibility is SEPARATE FROM ANCESTRY. An ordinary revert leaves the reverted
commit an ancestor of main for ever, so ancestry can never mean "a target anybody
still wants". A revoked commit is never promoted, by any path; a minimum safe
target is the floor below which nothing is promoted. Both are applied on every
promoting path, rollback included.
The approved combination, as EVIDENCE rather than literals. Each approved peer
revision is a RECEIPT under release/peers/, produced from that peer's own git by
node release/cli.mjs peer-receipt and pinned here by digest. The receipt's
contract values and capability levels are READ FROM THE PEER'S EXPORT FILES at
that revision; nothing in this file restates them.
SELECTION IS NOT SERVING. A receipt proves what a revision's SOURCE says; it
does not prove that revision is live. Serving is observed separately where a peer
publishes an identity, and refused by name where it does not.
CROSS-REPOSITORY CHANGES REMAIN AN ORDERED, MANUAL SEQUENCE. This gate is the only
path that consults this file: the backend's own deploy and the legacy
deploy-prod.yml make no compatibility decision. A new peer revision needs a new
receipt approved here in a reviewed pull request; an unchanged peer stays pinned.
The frontend's own commit is deliberately not pinned: a file cannot contain the
SHA of the commit that introduces it.

because the repository variable named here is not set.
MERGING CHANGES TO THIS DIRECTORY IS NOT INERT IN EVERY RESPECT, and saying so is

Setting the variable is NOT a cutover on its own: with deploy-prod.yml still

WHAT A NON-PUBLISHING EVALUATION MAY REPORT AS WAITING RATHER THAN FAILED.
Each entry is a pending commissioning prerequisite this policy itself records
as outstanding. A refusal made up of EXACTLY these, each standing in its
context (release/lib/readiness.mjs), from an AUTOMATIC deploy evaluation with
publication disabled, completes the evaluation without a red run. The DECISION
is unchanged: it is still REFUSE, allow:false, nothing is admitted and nothing
is published. Any other reason, any enabled or manual attempt, and any entry
whose prerequisite this policy records as resolved stays red.
The change that resolves a prerequisite removes its entry here in the same
reviewed change; committed-policy.test.mjs holds this list equal to what the
committed policy actually refuses.
